stories.title: Hdac3 shapes adipocyte size, death susceptibility, macrophage turnover, and vascular remodeling in a mouse model of obesity
stories.description: The crosstalk between adipocytes and macrophages is crucial in adipose tissue biology. The aim of this study was to investigate the role of adipocyte-expressed histone deacetylase 3 (Hdac3) on adipose tissue plasticity and immune cell composition in response to high-fat feeding. Here we show that adipocyte-specific deletion of Hdac3 gene in mice affects the response to high-fat overload, by reducing fat mass and adipocyte size in visceral fat of knockout mice. In the absence of adipocyte Hdac3, visceral fat shows vascular remodeling and increased macrophage content. Colocalization of F4/80 with Ki-67 indicates proliferation of resident macrophages. This is coupled with increased crown-like structures and adipocyte death in visceral fat of knockout mice, exacerbated by high-fat feeding. Hdac3 silencing in cultured adipocytes and inactivation in mice promotes a pro-apoptotic microenvironment, as assessed by positivity to Annexin V and cleaved Caspase 3. In conclusion, we propose that Hdac3 acts as a rheostat in visceral fat, differentially affecting lipid accumulation and adipocyte size during the progress of high fat diet (HFD) feeding, and limiting cell death, vascularization, and macrophage proliferation, in a mouse model of obesity.

stories.title: Prioritising emotional experience in pocket parks: towards human-centred design through Kano-based needs assessment
stories.description: As a key component of sustainable urban planning, the emotional design of pocket parks warrants further investigation. Drawing on case studies of four typical pocket parks in Shanghai and 400 valid questionnaire responses, this study developed emotional need indicators based on emotional design theory and combined the Kano model, Better–Worse coefficients, and non-parametric tests to classify and prioritise users’ emotional needs and examine differences across user groups. The results show that Must-be qualities, such as Safety and Security Assurance, establish the baseline conditions for use; One-dimensional qualities, such as Environmental Restorativeness, have a strong capacity to enhance satisfaction; and Attractive qualities, such as Social Interaction, foster deeper emotional experiences. Qualities such as Accessibility of Digital Services and Biodiversity were classified as Indifferent. Based on these needs priorities, this study proposes emotional design strategies that prioritise securing Must-be qualities, focus on developing One-dimensional qualities, and moderately expand Attractive qualities. The findings provide context-specific guidance for the design and renewal of pocket parks in Shanghai and other comparable high-density built environments, while offering empirical insights into the shift of public-space design from a function-oriented approach towards a human-centred and emotion-oriented approach.
